title: MaxPlace
description: MAXGEN 2.0 -- one MaxPlace document is one real place with its own history (its names, kinds, parent places and coordinates over time), each fact stored once as a claim with evidence so that many claims can point at it.

place_id.description: The place's permanent id: a random UUID created once by the writer (an import_file, resolve_conflict or build_tree task, R-24), never computed from a gazetteer or other outside id, and kept through renaming, re-typing and re-parenting.

redistribution_license.description: The licence under which this place document may be shared; when it is unclear, ask and never guess (RULES 7).

name_assertions.description: The names this place has had, at this level only (not the parent places), each a claim with its own evidence; at least one is required.

kind_assertions.description: What kind of place this was over time (a territory that became a state, a village that became a city), each a dated claim with its own evidence.

parent_place_assertions.description: The places this place lay inside over time, in one or more hierarchies (civil, church, judicial, census ...), each dated as closely as the evidence allows and each a claim with its own evidence; imported parents stay proposed.

coordinate_assertions.description: Where this place is on the earth, each with an uncertainty radius and its own evidence; several are allowed for places that moved.

related_place_assertions.description: Links to other places this one was formed from, split from, merged into, succeeded or preceded, each a dated claim with its own evidence; a new county or a split is a new place, linked here.

cited_record_ids.description: Records (MaxRecord ids) that are about the place as a whole, such as a parish history or a gazetteer page; research pointers kept beside the claims, each of which must exist (Appendix C).

media_refs.description: Maps and photographs of this place, pointed at by fingerprint on the record that holds each file (each file is described once, on the record that captured it).

is_private.description: True hides this place from anything shareable; it can only rise (the helper refuses lowering it), and a small place (street, address, building, farm, estate or of no stated kind) that a possibly living person's live claim points at is private at read time whatever this says.

name_claim.description: One name of this place, at this level only, from one piece of evidence; an imported full place string is kept word for word with name_type imported_full.

name_as_written.description: The place's name exactly as the evidence gives it.

lang.description: The language of the name (a BCP 47 tag such as en or de).

name_type.description: What kind of name this is; when no value fits, write other and give the words in name_type_as_written.

name_type_as_written.description: The source's or program's own words for the kind of name.

date.description: The period in which the place carried this name (a house renumbering becomes dated names).

is_preferred.description: True for the name to show first for this place.

kind_claim.description: What kind of place this was during one period, from one piece of evidence; kinds change over time.

kind.description: The kind of place (a ship may be a place of kind vessel); when no value fits, write other and give the words in kind_as_written or a published type in kind_uri.

kind_as_written.description: The source's or program's own words for the kind of place.

kind_uri.description: The address of the kind in a published vocabulary of place types, when there is one.

date.description: The period in which the place was of this kind.

parent_place_claim.description: One place this place lay inside, in one hierarchy, during one period, from one piece of evidence; whether a claim's written place names a jurisdiction that did not yet exist is worked out at read time from these.

parent_place_id.description: The MaxPlace this place lay inside; it must exist and be active when written (followed through merge redirects, Appendix C).

hierarchy.description: Which hierarchy this parent belongs to (a parish may sit in one county for civil purposes and another diocese for church purposes); when no value fits, write other and give the words in hierarchy_as_written.

hierarchy_as_written.description: The source's or program's own words for the hierarchy.

date.description: The period in which this place lay inside the parent, to the day when the evidence gives it (a county change partway through a year).

coordinate_claim.description: One position of this place on the earth, with its uncertainty, from one piece of evidence; several are allowed for places that moved.

latitude.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, north positive.

longitude.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, east positive.

uncertainty_m.description: The radius in metres within which the place lies, as far as the evidence allows; left out when the evidence states none (never invented), and the page then says 'precision not stated'.

uncertainty_as_written.description: What the evidence or the other program says about the precision, word for word (for example 'LatLongExact=0', or 'not stated').

date.description: The period in which the place stood at this position.

outline_uri.description: The address of an outline or boundary of the place (GEDCOM X spatialDescription), when there is one.

method_as_written.description: How the position was found, in the writer's or source's own words (read off a map, from a gazetteer, measured).

related_place_claim.description: One link from this place to another place it was formed from, split from, merged into, succeeded or preceded, from one piece of evidence.

relation.description: How this place is related to the other place; when no value fits, write other and give the words in relation_as_written.

relation_as_written.description: The source's own words for the relation.

place_id.description: The other MaxPlace; it must exist and be active when written (followed through merge redirects, Appendix C).

date.description: When the relation took effect (the date a county was formed or a town absorbed).
